job.title: Environmental Officer - Greenfield Mining Project
job.description:
About the opportunity

Stellar Recruitment is partnering with an Australian mining company to recruit an Environmental Officer for a greenfield critical minerals project near Mudgee.

This is an opportunity to join during the development phase and help establish the environmental systems, plans and processes that will support the project as it progresses. You’ll work within an experienced environmental team, with exposure to senior management and scope to develop your expertise across a broad range of environmental disciplines.

The project is progressing through the approvals process, with groundworks targeted for 2028, subject to approvals. The proposed mining operation involves a single open pit and day-shift mining, with substantial company-owned landholdings in the surrounding area.

About the role

Reporting to the Environmental Superintendent, you’ll combine environmental management system development with monitoring, reporting and biodiversity-related activities. Rather than simply maintaining established systems, you’ll have the opportunity to help build them.

A key focus will be developing practical management plans, procedures, forms, registers and processes, alongside supporting biodiversity management across the company’s properties.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Contributing to the development and implementation of the environmental management system.
  • Supporting biodiversity assessments, monitoring programs and management of biodiversity properties.
  • Coordinating environmental inspections and monitoring across water, air quality, noise, heritage and biodiversity.
  • Interpreting environmental data, preparing reports and supporting regulatory compliance.
  • Working with internal teams, consultants and contractors to translate environmental obligations into practical actions.
About you

You’ll be an environmental professional who enjoys variety, works well independently and is comfortable building relationships across different teams. Experience in mining is welcome, but backgrounds in resources, construction, infrastructure or a regulatory environment will also be considered.

Ideally, you’ll bring a relevant qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline, together with experience developing environmental management systems and interpreting environmental requirements. Strong written communication, organisation and stakeholder engagement skills will be important.

Experience managing biodiversity properties, coordinating biodiversity assessments or monitoring programs, and working with the NSW Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 will be particularly well regarded.

What’s on offer

An attractive remuneration package aligned with your experience, a supportive environmental team and the opportunity to broaden your expertise as the project develops.

You’ll work a 9-day fortnight, with accommodation available for the first six months to help you settle into the area. Set among rolling green hills and established rural communities, this opportunity would suit someone looking to build a career and a life in the Mudgee region.

Long-term residence in the area is required, although relocation does not need to happen immediately. There is flexibility to make the move over the first six to twelve months, allowing time to plan the transition.

How to apply

To express your interest, submit your resume through SEEK. For a confidential discussion about the role and relocation arrangements, contact the team at Stellar Recruitment.

job.description:

  • Attractive salary and benefits package
The operation:
  
George Fisher Mine (GFM) is a large-scale underground zinc-lead-silver operation based in Mt Isa, QLD. GFM has complex mining sequence, multiple operating fronts, and significant interactions among development, stoping, ventilation, backfill, infrastructure, services, and production readiness.
  
George Fisher has a long mine life and is a key strategic asset for Glencore globally.
  
The role:
  
The Senior Mining Engineer – Short Term Planning is responsible for leading and overseeing the preparation and delivery of short-term mine designs and plans to support the safe and efficient execution of development, production, services, and infrastructure activities
  
Your ability to translate medium- and long-term mine plans into practical short-term execution strategies aligned with operational capabilities and production targets will the crucial. We also need someone who can provide technical leadership and guidance to the mining engineering team and also optimise mine design / planning and drill and blast practices.
  
Experience required:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering or related subject
  • Minimum 6–8 years mining engineering experience, preferably within underground hard rock operations
  • Demonstrated experience in short-term mine planning, drill and blast design, and operational mine design.
  • Experience leading or mentoring engineering teams, graduates, or cadets.
  • Practical operational exposure with a strong understanding of underground mining methods and production processes.
  • Strong experience with mine design software such as Surpac, Vulcan, Datamine, or Deswik.
  • Advanced knowledge of drill and blast design, stope design, and operational mine planning.
Benefits on offer:
  • Permanent position working directly for Glencore.
  • Competitive salary package including 13% super, generous incentive scheme.
  • Access to training and professional development
  • Opportunity to work for a large mining company with opportunities to advance your career domestically and internationally.
  • Visa sponsorship available for suitability qualified candidates
  • FIFO to Mt Isa from Brisbane or Townsville or Mt Isa residential
Next Steps:
  
Glencore has partnered with Stellar Recruitment to manage the recruitment and search for this position. Please contact Lucas Eyers to discuss further or apply direct via email / SEEK / LinkedIn

lucas@stellarrecruitment.com.au

job.title: Human Resources Manager
job.description:
Harmony is the largest gold producer by volume in South Africa and is a significant operator of gold tailings retreatment facilities. CSA Mine has recently joined Harmony Australasia, marking the beginning of an exciting new chapter. The acquisition underpins Harmony’s strategy to expand its Australasian footprint and establish a strong, diversified copper portfolio, complemented by the Eva Copper Mine Project in Queensland, currently under construction, and set to become the state’s largest open‑pit copper mine upon commissioning. In Papua New Guinea, Harmony owns and operates the Hidden Valley mine and owns 50% of the Tier 1 Wafi-Golpu copper-gold project. These assets are supported by the Harmony Australasia regional corporate office located in Milton, Brisbane.
  
About The Role:

The Human Resources Manager – CSA Mine is responsible for delivering end‑to‑end HR leadership at the mine site. Working closely with and reporting to the site General Manager, this role supports safe and productive operations through effective workforce planning, industrial and employee relations, compliance with Australian employment legislation, and the development of a high‑performing workforce.
  
CSA Mine has a workforce of over 500 + contractors and there is also a site-based HR support team. The workforce consists of a mix of residential, DIDO and FIFO. 
  
Roster:
  
This role will be based onsite in Cobar, NSW working an 8/6-day FIFO roster from Brisbane or Sydney with local candidates highly regarded. Local candidates will be offered this opportunity on a 5/2 Monday to Friday roster.
  
Key Responsibilities:
  • Act as a trusted HR advisor to the Site General Manager and leadership team.
  • Deliver site‑based HR strategies aligned with operational and production objectives.
  • Translate corporate HR policies into practical site‑specific solutions.
  • Lead the onsite HR function, ensuring consistent and high‑quality service delivery.
  • Manage employee relations matters including performance management, grievances, investigations, and disciplinary processes.
  • Interpret and apply site enterprise agreements, awards, and contracts.

job.title: Design Manager
job.description:
Design Manager
Fortitude Valley, Brisbane | Permanent Full-Time

An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Design Manager with a strong interior design background to join a growing property and hospitality group based in Fortitude Valley.

This is not a traditional architecture-led Design Manager position. The business is looking for someone with creative flair, a strong eye for finishes, materials and spaces, and the ability to translate ideas into practical design outcomes across a diverse portfolio of hospitality, retail and accommodation assets.

Working closely with Project Managers and broader business stakeholders, you will help shape and maintain the design identity across the portfolio while also getting hands-on with smaller design projects.

The Role
As Design Manager, you will take ownership of design standards and provide creative design support across multiple business units and asset classes.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Create, refine and maintain design specifications and document libraries across the portfolio
  • Ensure consistency and compliance with agreed design standards across different asset classes
  • Undertake design reviews and provide recommendations across projects
  • Deliver smaller in-house design projects such as accommodation room and amenities refreshes
  • Support Project Managers with QA and defect reviews
  • Assist with RFIs relating to finishes, materials and design intent
  • Provide design advice across capital expenditure projects
  • Contribute to value management reviews, including alternative finishes and product selections
  • Balance design outcomes with practical cost considerations
  • Produce 3D elevations and visual concepts to support project presentations where required
About You
The key to this position is your interior design capability and creative eye. You may already hold a Design Manager title, or you could be a strong Interior Designer ready to step into a broader position.

Ideally, you will bring:
  • Formal qualifications in Interior Design or a related discipline
  • Strong experience across interior design, preferably within hospitality, hotels, retail or commercial environments
  • A strong eye for finishes, materials, colour, furniture and overall design aesthetic
  • Experience developing or maintaining design standards and specifications
  • Ability to review designs and confidently provide creative input and direction
  • Understanding of project budgets and the cost implications of design decisions
  • Experience working alongside Project Managers, contractors and suppliers
  • Capability with relevant design and 3D visualisation software
  • A practical, collaborative approach with the confidence to take ownership of design decisions
Importantly, the business is not looking for someone who is heavily architecture or technically focused. They are looking for someone who brings genuine artistic flair and interior design sensibility, while still understanding how their ideas translate into real-world projects.

If you are an experienced Interior Designer or Design Manager looking to move into a broader client-side environment where your creativity will be genuinely valued, we would love to hear from you. Reach out to Monique @ Stellar

This is a pivotal role sitting within the compliance function, responsible for owning and driving all emergency response capability across site.

Reporting into the Compliance Manager, you’ll take the lead on ensuring emergency systems, teams and equipment are not just compliant but genuinely fit for purpose in a modern underground mining environment.

job.title: Senior Project Engineer (Marine Piling)
job.description:
About the Company
  
Firmly positioned in Western Australia and nationally as a high-quality, mid-tier civil and marine contracting business, this company is flying in the current market. They have strong financial backing and an impressive sustainable business as they are aligned with several blue-chip mining companies and key public sector clients. They now have an IMMEDIATE need to appoint a SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER in their high-performance WA team.
  
About the Role
  
As SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER you will work FIFO 2/1 ex-Perth, to support construction delivery of a large marine project for a blue-chip mining client on WA’s coast. This project will involve multidisciplinary elements of Civil, SMP and electrical works plus marine piling and steel erection being undertaken from a jack-up barge. The SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER will support the delivery of this multi-disciplinary package of marine construction works by providing technical guidance and coordination planning for the construction delivery team. Also you will lead and mentor younger engineers, and ensure adherence to financial, and contractual parameters. This will involve programming & scheduling the works, planning and reviewing heavy lift studies, weekly and monthly reporting, “cost to complete” forecasting and managing budgets. If you possess proven experience in a similar SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER/Project Engineer role on marine/piling/structural steel erection projects in an industrial construction environment, you can expect an attractive remuneration package of CIRCA $290K+. This business is also "preferred" status on other marine projects, and tendering multiple upcoming major projects so are well placed to support your career long term. 
  
Skills, Qualifications and Other Requirements
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil/Structural/Mechanical Engineering
  • 7+ years’ post graduate construction experience as Project Engineer/SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER for civil/marine contractors in Australia
  • Previous experience managing marine piling and structural steel erection from construction and jack-up barges for jetties, wharves, mooring dolphins, marine load-out facilities or other marine structures
  • Strong contractual and commercial acumen
  • Willingness and ability to undertake 2/1 FIFO roster (ex-Perth)
  • Natural leadership skills and ability to manage client interface
  • WA based with existing rights to work in Australia
  • Available within 4 weeks’ notice period

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
About Harmony:
Harmony is the largest gold producer by volume in South Africa and is a significant operator of gold tailings retreatment facilities. In Papua New Guinea, Harmony owns and operates the Hidden Valley mine and owns 50% of the Tier 1 Wafi-Golpu copper-gold project. In Australia, Harmony owns the high-grade CSA copper mine in Cobar, NSW and is constructing the Eva Copper Mine in Cloncurry, QLD. These assets are supported by the Harmony Australasia regional corporate office located in Milton, Brisbane.
  
The Eva Copper Mine is a significant and strategically important project for Harmony marking a major milestone in the company’s copper growth strategy and its long-term commitment to Northwest Queensland. The mine will have a minimum life of 15 years and will involve mining multiple open cut pits providing copper bearing ore to a concentrator. Front-end engineering design is complete, and mine construction is expected to take up to 30 months with first production targeted for the second half of the 2028 calendar year.
  
About the role:
An opportunity exists for a Safety Advisor to join a growing site-based team in Cloncurry, North West Queensland. Reporting to the Senior Safety and Training Advisor, this role provides hands-on field safety support across both construction and operational activities, ensuring compliance with site health and safety systems while positively influencing frontline safety behaviours.
  
This position will suit a Safety Advisor who enjoys being visible in the field, engaging with crews and supervisors and contributing to the development of a strong, values-driven safety culture on a new and evolving project.
  
This role will be DIDO from local communities or FIFO from Brisbane or Townsville to our site in Cloncurry NW QLD, with local candidates highly regarded. Local employees are paid a regional allowance and a competitive salary. Roster is 14 days on, 7 days off.
  
Please note this is a fixed term role aligned with the project completion and close out, anticipated to be 31 May 2028. However, there is a possibility the role could become a permanent position once the mine is fully operational.
  
Key Responsibilities:
  • Provide field safety support in line with the Safety and Health Management System
  • Assist with site inductions, access control and training compliance
  • Support supervisors with competency assessments and workforce development
  • Assist with incident investigations and emergency response activities
  • Promote safe work practices and intervene where unsafe behaviours are identified
  • Maintain accurate safety and training records
Experience Required:
  • Minimum 2 years’ health and safety experience, ideally in mining
  • Strong knowledge of health and safety legislation
  • Current QLD manual driver’s licence
  • Current First Aid qualification
  • Strong communication and organisational skills
  • Safety qualifications and DoneSafe experience desirable
Why Join Us:
  • An opportunity to be part of a formidable team focused on building an exciting, new project.
  • Eligible to participate in the company bonus scheme.
  • Highly competitive remuneration, incentives, and other benefits.
  • Corporate / discounted rates with Medibank and Qantas Club.
  • Access to Harmony's benefits discounts scheme.
  • Harmony is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.
  • Work for a company who values their employees and recognises their contribution
Next Steps:
Stellar Recruitment is pleased to be assisting Harmony with the project ramp up. Please apply via SEEK and Rob Gantly will get in touch with you early 2026 to walk you through next steps and answer any questions you may have.

job.title: Manager Health, Safety, Environment, Risk & Training
job.description:
About the opportunity
Stellar Recruitment is partnering with South32 to recruit a Manager Health, Safety, Environment, Risk & Training for Cannington Mine in northwest Queensland.

Reporting directly to the Vice President Operations, you will lead the site’s health and hygiene, safety, material risk, environment, training, emergency response and compliance functions. You will lead an established multidisciplinary team of approximately 21 people and serve as a key member of Cannington’s senior leadership team.

The technical foundations are established. The opportunity is to provide clear direction, strengthen leadership capability and accountability, and ensure priority programs of work are implemented effectively and sustained. Success will require a leader who can establish expectations, constructively challenge missed commitments, simplify priorities and consistently translate plans into operational outcomes.

This is a visible operational leadership role. You will work closely with leaders across the mine to strengthen ownership of health, safety, material risk, environment and workforce competency within the line organisation.

Key responsibilities
  • Lead, coach and develop the HSERT leadership team, creating a culture of care, accountability, constructive challenge and consistent delivery.
  • Set a clear strategic direction and focused annual operating plan across health and hygiene, safety, material risk, environment and training.
  • Translate strategy, assurance findings and improvement priorities into executable programs with clear accountabilities, milestones and measures of success.
  • Establish disciplined governance and follow-through, ensuring critical actions and commitments are completed to the required standard and timeframe.
  • Influence, coach and constructively challenge senior operational leaders to strengthen line ownership of safety, risk and workforce capability.
  • Provide visible field leadership and help leaders improve the quality of critical control management, operational routines and risk-based decision-making.
  • Strengthen material risk management, critical control verification, hazard identification, incident management and significant-event investigation.
  • Lead change across the HSERT function, including simplifying systems and redirecting specialist effort toward the activities that most effectively reduce risk and improve operational performance.
  • Oversee regulatory compliance, environmental approvals and reporting across the mine and associated rail and port activities.
  • Provide strategic leadership across health and hygiene, injury management, workers compensation, emergency response and training systems.
  • Build trusted, transparent relationships with operational leaders, corporate functions, contractors, regulators and external service providers.
  • Manage the function’s budget, performance reporting and improvement portfolio, connecting technical requirements with practical operational and commercial decisions.
About you
You are an experienced mining or heavy-industry leader who combines credible HSERT judgement with strong people leadership, operational influence and disciplined execution.

The strongest candidates will demonstrate:
  • Leadership of complex teams: At least five years’ experience leading a multidisciplinary team of 10 or more people, including senior technical or functional leaders.
  • Delivery and change leadership: A strong record of implementing significant change and delivering complex programs of work through clear priorities, effective governance and sustained follow-through.
  • Accountability and performance: Demonstrated ability to establish clear expectations, address missed commitments and improve team performance while maintaining trust and engagement.
  • Operational influence: The credibility and confidence to coach, influence and constructively challenge senior operational leaders, contractors, technical specialists and frontline teams.
  • Material risk leadership: Sound operational understanding of material risk, critical controls, significant-event management, regulatory compliance and management-system effectiveness.
  • Breadth across the HSERT portfolio: Sufficient exposure to environment, health and hygiene, emergency response and training to lead specialist expertise and make balanced, risk-based decisions.
  • Commercial judgement: Experience managing budgets and prioritising technical requirements, risk-reduction initiatives and business needs in a resource-constrained operational environment.
  • Communication and stakeholder leadership: Advanced communication, facilitation and influencing capability, including engagement with executives, regulators and workforce representatives.
  • Relevant qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in science, engineering, safety or a related discipline. Postgraduate qualifications in work health and safety will be highly regarded.
  • Roster flexibility: The ability to work a 4 days on, 3 days off roster and occasionally participate in an 8 days on, 6 days off duty-manager swing.
Why Cannington?
Cannington is a large, established underground base-metals operation offering the scale, complexity and operational exposure expected of a senior mining leadership role.

The position offers direct access to the Vice President Operations and genuine authority across the complete HSERT portfolio. You will inherit technically capable specialists and have the opportunity to strengthen alignment, leadership capability, accountability and execution across both the function and the broader operation.

This role will suit a senior leader who wants to make a visible operational impact, build a stronger team and deliver meaningful, sustained improvement in health, safety, risk, environment and workforce capability.

Benefits
  • Attractive 4 days on, 3 days off roster
  • Established multidisciplinary team of approximately 21 people
  • Broad influence across the complete HSERT portfolio
  • Senior position within Cannington’s operational leadership team
  • Competitive salary package
  • 14% superannuation contributions
  • Annual short-term incentive
If you are a senior mining or heavy-industry leader who combines strong judgement with visible, accountable people leadership and a proven ability to turn plans into sustained results, we welcome a confidential discussion.

For further information, contact Rob Gantly or Lucas Eyers at Stellar Recruitment, or select Apply Now to submit your application.

This opportunity sits within an established Auckland law practice with a strong focus on property transactions and long-term client relationships.

The team acts for a mix of private individuals, investors, developers and commercial clients across a wide range of property matters. Lawyers are encouraged to take ownership of their work, maintain direct client contact and build trusted professional relationships from an early stage.

For an experienced property lawyer seeking greater responsibility, stronger client ownership and the ability to influence the direction of a growing practice, this role offers a compelling next step.

job.description:
We are looking for a capable Surveyor to join a stable, well-regarded WA surveying team. They are a great WA Survey business with around 20 employees, have low staff turnover, and work with repeat clients who regularly ask for their surveyors by name. The work is mainly civil and infrastructure surveying across Main Roads projects, local government and shires, major contractors and private clients. Around 60% of their workload is directly engaged government work, giving their team a strong pipeline and genuine continuity between projects, but they also have several key clients in the resources sector offering greenfields minesite project work.

About the role

As Surveyor you will work across a mix of Perth metro, Wheatbelt and regional WA projects, with occasional FIFO/DIDO assignments in areas such as the Pilbara, Goldfields, Mid West and Kimberley. Locally based work is generally within four hours of Perth, with typical full-time staff working around 50 hours per week when local workloads are busy. So if you are a capable Surveyor looking for variety in work and types of projects, this could be the place for you. 

What’s on offer?
  • Stable, ongoing employment with work beyond individual project end dates
  • Supportive team culture with low turnover and repeat clients
  • Metro rate of circa $60/hr + super
  • 30% overtime uplift above 38 hours Monday-Friday and on weekends for local work
  • 40% uplift for Pilbara, Goldfields, Mid West and Kimberley work
  • FIFO assignments are on 2/1 rosters, 10-12 hours per day
  • A mix of office-based continuity, DIDO/FIFO project work and regular return-to-base employment
About you
  • You can complete survey calculations confidently and accurately
  • You know how to carry out "conventional surveys" properly, not just collect data
  • You can produce a clear, coherent report explaining what you did
  • You value long-term stability and being part of a team, not just chasing the next project
  • You are comfortable being away when the work is there and working from the Perth office between projects
  • You are competent using Leica Total Stations, 12D or Carlsen software
  • You have a great attitude, capacity to learn and problem-solving ability

job.title: Procurement Manager
job.description:
Our Client:

Our client is a well-established and growing nationwide organisation, operating within the commercial construction sector. With a strong focus on quality, innovation, operational excellence, and customer satisfaction, the business is investing in its procurement capability to support continued growth.
This newly created position offers an experienced procurement professional the opportunity to take ownership of international sourcing, strengthen established supplier partnerships, and develop new supply channels across global markets.

About the Role:

As Procurement Manager, you will lead procurement activity across a wide range of construction and building products. You will manage and strengthen existing offshore supplier relationships while identifying new manufacturing and trade partnerships that improve commercial performance, product quality, and supply chain resilience.
Working closely with Regional Managers, Project Managers, senior leaders, finance, logistics partners, and international suppliers, you will oversee the complete procurement process, from sourcing and negotiation through to product testing, compliance, freight coordination, and delivery into New Zealand.
This is an autonomous position requiring strong commercial judgement, cultural awareness, and the confidence to establish trusted relationships across diverse international markets.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Manage, establish, and strengthen international supplier and manufacturing relationships
  • Identify and evaluate new offshore suppliers, products, and global sourcing opportunities
  • Lead sourcing, tendering, pricing reviews, contract negotiations, and commercial agreements
  • Coordinate product testing, compliance documentation, quality standards, and supplier warranties
  • Oversee international freight, shipping schedules, customs processes, and delivery into NZ
  • Partner with Regional and Project Managers to forecast demand, manage supply risks, and maintain product availability
Skills and Experience:
  • At least five years of procurement experience, ideally within building products, construction supply, manufacturing, or merchant environments
  • Proven experience managing offshore suppliers and developing international sourcing relationships
  • Strong commercial negotiation, strategic sourcing, contract management, and supplier evaluation capability
  • Practical knowledge of international logistics, freight, customs, product testing, and supply chain risk
  • Confident communication, analytical, reporting, relationship management, and cross cultural collaboration skills
  • A current passport and willingness to travel internationally, with additional language capability advantageous but not essential
This is a high impact position for a self motivated procurement professional who enjoys working independently, developing trusted supplier relationships, and delivering measurable commercial value. You will have the opportunity to influence procurement strategy while contributing directly to the growth and resilience of a progressive construction organisation.

How to Apply:

If you thrive on developing global supplier relationships and identifying new commercial opportunities, we would welcome your application.
Apply online. Applications will be acknowledged within five working days. For a confidential conversation, please contact Fiona Sanderson on 03 222 2304 or email fiona.s@stellarrecruitment.co.nz.
Please note, only New Zealand residents or citizens will be considered for this permanent position.

Big Yellow is looking for experienced mining operators and operators from relevant industries such as forestry, civil, heavy-road transport and agriculture to step into a FIFO role to Perth, Western Australia. job.title: STMS
job.description:
Looking for an experienced Site Traffic Management Supervisor (STMS) to lead traffic management operations on site.

This role suits someone who takes ownership of site safety, communicates clearly, and understands the responsibility that comes with supervising traffic control on active civil sites. You’ll be trusted to run traffic management properly, support your team, and maintain high standards at all times.


What you’ll be doing
  • Leading and supervising traffic management on civil construction sites
  • Implementing and maintaining approved Traffic Management Plans (TMPs)
  • Briefing and overseeing Traffic Controllers on site
  • Ensuring all traffic control measures meet NZTA and site requirements
  • Liaising with site supervisors, councils, and contractors
  • Monitoring compliance, safety, and site conditions throughout the day
  • Managing site documentation and traffic management records

What good looks like here
  • Turning up prepared and running the site from the start
  • Setting clear expectations with your traffic control team
  • Identifying and addressing risks before they become issues
  • Communicating calmly and clearly under pressure
  • Maintaining compliance without cutting corners
  • Leaving sites safe, controlled, and audit ready

Required experience and tickets These are required and are a barrier to entry:
  • Current Practicing STMS qualification
  • Proven experience supervising traffic management on civil sites
  • Strong understanding of TMPs and traffic management requirements
  • ConstructSafe or Site Safe
  • Full Class 1 Drivers License required, Class 2 beneficial
Highly regarded:
  • Experience on roading or large scale infrastructure projects
  • Leadership or mentoring experience
  • Additional traffic management or civil tickets

What’s in it for you
  • Competitive pay based on experience
  • Consistent hours with a strong pipeline of projects
  • Well organised sites with clear communication
  • A role with real responsibility and trust
  • Support from a recruiter who understands traffic management and civil construction
Next steps If you’re an experienced STMS who takes pride in running safe, compliant sites and leading your team properly, we should talk. Apply now for a confidential chat.

You must be legally entitled to work in New Zealand. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted directly.

job.title: Legal Counsel
job.description:
About the Role
This is a rare opportunity to step into a sole counsel role within a diversified property and investment business.

Working directly with senior leadership, you'll provide advice across commercial property, leasing, disputes, governance, compliance and wider business initiatives. Your role will extend beyond technical legal support, with regular involvement in commercial discussions, project work and matters that influence business outcomes.

The work is broad, commercially focused and highly visible. You'll be exposed to everything from day-to-day operational issues through to acquisitions, development projects, dispute resolution and strategic business decisions.

For a lawyer who enjoys variety and wants to be part of the decision-making process rather than reviewing matters from the sidelines, this role offers significant breadth and engagement.

Key Work
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements
  • Advising on leasing, licensing and commercial property matters
  • Supporting acquisitions, disposals and development projects
  • Managing disputes, claims and contentious matters
  • Providing legal advice on risk, governance and compliance issues
  • Partnering with senior stakeholders on strategic initiatives
  • Managing relationships with external legal advisers
  • Supporting legal operations and process improvement
  • Assisting with financing, investment and transactional activity
The work is varied and business-facing, requiring the ability to switch between operational matters and higher-level commercial projects.  

About You:
  • NZ qualified lawyer with approximately 6+ years PQE
  • Strong commercial property, leasing and transactional experience
  • Experience drafting and negotiating complex commercial agreements
  • Sound judgement and a pragmatic approach to legal risk
  • Confidence engaging directly with senior stakeholders
  • Strong commercial awareness and business acumen
  • Ability to prioritise effectively across multiple matters
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to provide practical recommendations
Lawyers from property, commercial or real estate-focused practices are likely to find the transition particularly relevant. However, candidates with a blend of private practice and in-house experience will also be considered.  

The Opportunity
Many legal counsel roles focus on a single business unit or operate within larger legal teams.

This role offers something broader.

As the sole legal adviser, you'll gain exposure across a wide range of legal and commercial issues while working closely with the people responsible for the direction of the business. Your advice will contribute to decisions involving property, investment, operational and strategic matters, providing variety that is often difficult to find in more specialised roles.

The breadth of work will appeal to lawyers who enjoy applying their legal expertise across multiple disciplines while remaining closely connected to the commercial realities of the business.

What Success Looks Like
This is a fast-paced commercial environment where priorities can shift quickly, and legal advice is expected to be practical, commercially aware and clearly communicated.

Success in the role comes from developing a strong understanding of the business, maintaining momentum across multiple matters and exercising sound judgement when balancing risk, opportunity and commercial objectives. You'll work closely with senior decision-makers who value clear recommendations, thoughtful analysis and a solutions-focused approach.

The breadth of work, visibility across the organisation and pace of decision-making will appeal to lawyers who enjoy responsibility, variety and a broad mix of legal and commercial challenges.

About the Business
This established Auckland-based business owns, manages and invests in a substantial portfolio of commercial assets and related ventures.

The legal function supports a broad range of activities across property, investment and operational matters, creating exposure that extends well beyond a traditional property law role.

The result is a role that combines technical legal work with genuine commercial involvement, allowing the successful lawyer to become a trusted adviser across the wider business.

How to Apply
Click "QUICK APPLY" or send your CV & Aacademic Transcripts to jenny.g@stellarrecruitment.co.nz, or for a confidential chat, call Jenny on 021 0230 3960.

Please include your academic transcript with your CV, as this forms part of the initial review.

job.title: Executive Manager - Operational Excellence
job.description:
About the company:

Enaex is a world leader in industrial-grade ammonium nitrate production and a leading provider of integrated rock fragmentation services in Latin America and beyond, operating in over 40 countries worldwide.

Enaex Australia has more than 20 years of experience delivering blasting services across open-pit and underground mining, supporting multiple commodities including iron ore, gold, and coal. With a fleet of Mobile Processing Units, five advanced emulsion-manufacturing facilities, and a workforce of approximately 350 skilled professionals, they combine local expertise with global knowledge to provide safe, efficient, and innovative blasting solutions.

The opportunity:

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this is a broad and influential leadership position responsible for bringing together the HSE, Asset Management / Maintenance, Engineering, Training, Bulk Products & Regulatory Compliance functions to support safe, reliable and compliant operations across the business.

As Executive Manager – Operational Excellence, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of senior technical and professional leaders with responsibility across several business-critical areas.

A particular focus of the position is the stewardship and safe operation of Enaex Australia's emulsion manufacturing plants classified as Major Hazard Facilities (MHF). You will play a key role in maintaining strong relationships with regulators and ensuring the business continues to meet its regulatory, licensing and operating obligations.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing executive leadership across relevant department
  • Leading safety, risk and compliance frameworks across the organisation
  • Holding senior accountability for Major Hazard Facility obligations, regulatory engagement and operating approvals
  • Ensuring the integrity, reliability and availability of critical physical assets including fleet, MPUs, manufacturing plant and associated infrastructure
  • Driving asset management / maintenance strategies that improve plant uptime, operational reliability and production continuity.
  • Leading and supporting asset upgrades, engineering improvements and management-of-change initiatives
  • Overseeing quality assurance and continuous improvement of bulk explosive and emulsion products
  • Translating customer and commercial challenges into safe, compliant and operationally viable technical solutions
  • Working closely with the COO and operational leadership to ensure asset readiness supports current and future operational requirements.
  • Providing the CEO and senior leadership with clear visibility of asset risk, safety performance, regulatory matters and major investment requirements
  • Building credible and constructive relationships with regulators, industry bodies and other external stakeholders
  • Leading experienced technical and professional teams through operational change and continuous improvement.
About you:

This position will suit a highly experienced executive who combines strong operational judgement with technical credibility and the ability to lead across multiple disciplines.

You will ideally bring:
  • 20+ years' relevant industry experience, including significant senior leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated experience working within highly regulated, high-risk industrial environments.
  • Direct exposure to Major Hazard Facilities or equivalent highly regulated critical assets
  • Experience engaging with regulators through audits, licensing processes, regulatory reviews and approvals.
  • A strong understanding of operational risk, safety, asset management / maintenance and business continuity
  • Proven experience leading multidisciplinary technical and professional teams.
  • Experience delivering asset upgrades, operational change and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • The ability to balance safety, regulatory, operational, technical and commercial priorities.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence at executive, operational and regulatory levels.
  • A leadership style that develops experienced professionals, builds accountability and creates high-performing teams.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in business management or a related discipline, with postgraduate or master’s level qualifications viewed favourably.
The position is ideally Brisbane based and will require regular travel across Australia. Consideration may also be given for Perth based candidates – although the travel component if based here may be higher.

A competitive salary package is on offer to attract the right candidate.

For further information or to formally apply please contact Lucas Eyers at Stellar Recruitment for a confidential discussion.

You will lead a multidisciplinary team across Mechanical, Electrical, Civil and Structural engineering, working closely with Maintenance, Reliability, Operations and Technical stakeholders to identify opportunities, develop project strategies and deliver outcomes that support the long-term performance of the operation.

You will play a key role in ensuring fabrication and welding activities are completed to the highest standards, while driving continuous improvement across the company's quality processes.

  • Support internal and external quality audits
  • Assist with non-conformance investigations and corrective actions
  
About You
To be successful in this role, you will need to have:
  • AS/NZS 2214 Welding Inspector qualification, or equivalent
  • Alternatively, AS 1796 Certificate 10 or similar welding inspection certification
  • Proven experience in welding and fabrication inspection
  • Experience inspecting structural steel, piping systems, pressure piping, or heavy fabrication
  • Strong understanding of welding standards and quality requirements
  • Experience with WPS/PQRs, welder qualifications, weld maps and inspection records
  • Experience operating or managing an ISO 9001 Quality Management System

job.description:

  • Highly attractive salary package on a 9-day fortnight roster
  • Owner operated company that puts people first and values growth and flexibility
About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Mining Engineer to join us at our Boggabri mine, an open-cut coal operation producing more than 7 million tonnes per annum, and with a mine life extending through until 2036. Boggabri mine is located near Boggabri, Gunnedah and Narrabri, regional towns which offer community spirit and a unique and diverse country lifestyle.
  
The Senior Mining Engineer provides specialist engineering expertise across short-term mine planning, drill and blast, and operational design activities to support safe and efficient coal mining operations. The role leads a team of Mining Engineers, Drill and Blast Engineers, Graduates and Technical Officers, providing technical direction, coaching and day-to-day leadership while ensuring work is aligned with operational priorities and business objectives.

On offer is a range of benefits including:
  • Attractive salary plus housing allowance
  • Monday to Friday roster with option for 9-day fortnight
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • Annual performance bonus structure - STIP
  • Paid parental leave.
  • Career progression and training opportunities
  • Education assistance
  • A relocation assistance package to beautiful country NSW
About you:

You believe in fostering a positive, collaborative work culture - ensuring we always put our people first.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in Mining Engineering or related subject
  • Significant experience in open cut mining engineering, preferably within the coal industry
  • Demonstrated expertise in mine planning, scheduling, drill and blast design and operational support
  • Experience leading and mentoring technical professionals within a mining environment
  • Strong understanding of mining legislation, safety systems and environmental compliance requirements.
  • Well-developed analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience with a range of mine planning and scheduling software applications like Vulcan, SPRY, Deswik, Gantt Scheduler, Talpac etc
Working at Idemitsu:

Idemitsu Australia has been operating in Australia since 1978 and is a subsidiary of Idemitsu Kosan, based in Tokyo. Committed to sustainability and innovation, Idemitsu Australia continues to meet energy demands through supply of high-quality metallurgical and thermal coal, while we actively diversify and decarbonise our energy portfolio. Idemitsu has a strong focus on its people, demonstrated through our unique culture, together with competitive compensation, professional growth and a flexible work environment.

Come and join an energy solutions company that values inclusiveness and sustainability, with a commitment to its people, the environment and society.

You can find out more at www.idemitsu.com.au

job.title: Production Engineer
job.description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Manufacturing-focused engineer responsible for optimising site operations, driving best-practice precast manufacturing processes, and ensuring safe, efficient, high quality production. You will be responsible for leading technical support, process improvement and project delivery while improving productivity, cost, quality and delivery performance. You will also promote a positive Health and Safety culture. You duties will include:
  • Promote and maintain a strong safety-first culture across the site
  • Interpret shop drawings and manufacturing standards (NZS3101, NZS3109, NZS4058)
  • Develop and maintain SOPs for safe and accurate precast manufacture
  • Provide technical direction to the team for reinforcement, moulds, penetrations, pours, curing, lifting and finishing
  • Use CAD to review/edit drawings and support manufacturing accuracy
  • Ensure all drawings, materials, moulds, plant and labour are ready to meet production plans and customer expectations
  • Monitor WIP, output, downtime, waste and rework
  • Drive continuous improvement in QC/QA, reporting and production systems
  • Attend pre-start checks and toolbox talks and be a regular voice for the team
  • Ensuring adequate resources are available for effective execution of the production plan
  • Coaching and developing the team members
This roster is Monday – Friday based, however at the moment Saturday mornings will also be required as the team are extremely busy! The role is based in Pokeno. This role is on a permanent basis and we are looking for somebody who wants to stay long-term and is interesting in progressing within the company. There are options for you to progress into a senior management role fairly quickly.

Skills & Experience

Due to the nature of the role, to be successful in this role you will need:
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Civil or Construction Engineering (or equivalent)
  • Minimum 3 years experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Experience in process improvement, problem-solving and production engineering
  • Experience in a concrete manufacturing facility is preferred
  • Effective communication skills and ability to be a decision-maker
  • Good leadership and people management skills
  • Strong IT skills – you will be working on computers daily
  • Excellent understanding of Health & Safety procedures
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings
  • To be able to pass a Drug & Alcohol test
  • A great attitude and willingness to learn
About the Company

We are a leader in New Zealand in Water Management Products. We operate eight factory sites across New Zealand and we supply product types for drainage, watermain, environmental. We are proudly family-owned and we were founded 50 years ago and have grown significantly, with now more than 800 employees. We are a proven leader in our market!
